questions.stem: What is the key difference between sexual and asexual reproduction?

options.text: Sexual reproduction is faster than asexual reproduction
Sexual reproduction involves the fusion of gametes; asexual does not

questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction involves the fusion of two gametes (sex cells) from two parents, producing genetically varied offspring. Asexual reproduction involves only one parent and no fusion of gametes, producing genetically identical offspring (clones).

questions.stem: What type of cell division produces gametes?
questions.explanation: Meiosis is the type of cell division that produces gametes (sex cells). It halves the chromosome number, so each gamete contains half the normal number of chromosomes. When two gametes fuse at fertilisation, the full number is restored.

questions.stem: Which is an advantage of sexual reproduction over asexual reproduction?

options.text: It produces genetic variation in offspring

questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction produces genetic variation because offspring receive a unique combination of alleles from both parents. This variation is important for natural selection and helps populations adapt to changing environments.

questions.stem: What are the offspring of asexual reproduction called?
questions.explanation: Offspring produced by asexual reproduction are genetically identical to the parent and to each other, so they are called clones. This is because asexual reproduction involves mitosis, which copies DNA exactly.

questions.stem: Which of the following organisms can reproduce asexually?
questions.explanation: Bacteria reproduce asexually by binary fission, splitting into two identical cells. Many other organisms can also reproduce asexually, including plants (by runners or tubers) and some animals like starfish and hydra.

questions.stem: What is an advantage of asexual reproduction?

options.text: It is rapid and requires only one parent
It helps populations adapt to new diseases
It requires the fusion of gametes
It produces lots of genetic variation

questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction is rapid because it does not require finding a mate, and only one parent is needed. This allows organisms to colonise new environments quickly and produce large numbers of offspring when conditions are favourable.

questions.stem: How many chromosomes do human gametes contain?
questions.explanation: Human gametes (sperm and egg cells) contain 23 chromosomes, which is half the normal body cell number of 46. When a sperm and egg fuse at fertilisation, the resulting zygote has the full set of 46 chromosomes.
